summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, hypertension, and congestive heart failure was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and fluid overload after missing a dialysis session. His symptoms included orthopnea, fatigue, leg swelling, and postprandial vomiting. Imaging showed bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary congestion consistent with heart failure exacerbation. He underwent hemodialysis, which improved his respiratory status and volume overload. His nausea was evaluated with a CT scan, which showed no obstruction, and was attributed to GERD. He was discharged stable on room air with medication adjustments, including discontinuation of pioglitazone and insulin dose reduction, and instructions to initiate CPAP therapy for sleep apnea.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
